verdict: PPG grew sales 7% to $4.4B on higher prices and volumes — led by aerospace and protective coatings — and earned a record third-quarter profit per share, even as raw-material inflation squeezed its industrial coatings margins.

segments.name: Global Architectural Coatings
segments.note: House paints and building coatings — Latin America led, with higher prices in every region.

segments.name: Performance Coatings
segments.note: Aerospace, protective & marine and car-repair (refinish) coatings — aerospace grew double digits and its order backlog stayed near $300M.

segments.name: Industrial Coatings
segments.note: Coatings for car factories, packaging and general industry — the biggest segment, with packaging up double digits on share gains.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling paint and running the company day to day, including $92M of corporate expenses.

opex.name: Depreciation
opex.note: Wear and tear on factories and equipment, spread over their useful lives.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new coatings and specialty products.

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Writing down the value of brands and technology bought in past acquisitions.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $22M (interest expense of $67M less interest income of $45M), partly offset by $5M of other income — a net $17M drag.
footerNote: Net income here is the $478M from continuing operations including noncontrolling interests; $473M was attributable to PPG shareholders. Including a $22M loss from discontinued operations, total net income attributable to PPG was $451M.
follow100Note: Kept-as-profit is profit from continuing operations, including the small share belonging to noncontrolling interests. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Performance Coatings led
takeaways.text: Segment sales rose 10% to $1.55B with organic growth of 8%, led by aerospace, protective & marine and refinish coatings. Its profit margin (EBITDA) widened to 23.9% of sales.

takeaways.title: Architectural margins jumped
takeaways.text: Global Architectural Coatings' EBITDA margin rose 3 points to 24.0% of sales on Latin American strength, higher prices and cost cuts, even though paint volumes dipped slightly.

takeaways.title: Industrial lagged
takeaways.text: Industrial Coatings' EBITDA fell 11% and its margin shrank to 14.4% as raw-material inflation outran price increases — the one soft spot, despite double-digit growth in packaging coatings.

oneTimers: Adjusted EPS of $2.25 (non-GAAP) excludes $20M of acquisition-related amortization, $11M of restructuring costs and smaller items; GAAP EPS from continuing operations was $2.12.
A business PPG is exiting lost $22M after tax in discontinued operations, which is why total net income attributable to PPG ($451M) is lower than the continuing-operations figure used in the chart.
